ui.portada_sub: La Jauría’s all-in-one for World of Warcraft: Forever
ui.hecho_por: Made by toxic3000 for La Jauría

parrafos: Alfa is La Jauría’s all-in-one for World of Warcraft: Forever. It brings your route and guides, the map, bags, talents, encyclopedia, dungeons, healing, fishing, trading and your pack together in one addon, all with the same look and in your language. It needs no other addon.

Alfa doesn’t play for you: it keeps you company. The first time, it asks you one question at a time what you want it to do on its own, and you decide everything else. In combat it never presses anything for you; it only shows you what’s worth doing.
This manual walks you through every part of Alfa, with screenshots, steps and tips. Read it straight through or jump from the contents to whatever interests you: each chapter stands on its own.
carta.lya: Hi! I’m Lya, the pack’s she-wolf. I’ll keep you company through the whole manual and in the game too. If you ever get lost, give me a click and I’ll lend you a paw… and if you bring a sausage, even better.

items.texto: Open **Instalar-Alfa.exe** and let it find your game.
Two minutes to decide what Alfa does for you.
Your window, with everything one click away. Let’s play!

como_leer.texto: Green numbers are steps: follow them in order.
Ideas to get more out of Alfa.
[[M]] is a key; `/alfa` is typed in chat.
What changes or arrives in a version.

partes.lema: Install Alfa, set it up your way and meet your new window.

capitulos.lema: From zero to playing with Alfa in a few minutes.

bloques.texto: Installing Alfa takes a minute, and setting it up about two more. Here are the two ways to install it, what happens the first time you enter the game and how to keep it up to date.
Install with Instalar-Alfa.exe (the easy way)

pasos: Checks which version is the newest.
Finds your WoW Forever on its own.
Downloads Alfa, checks it and copies it.

bloques.pie: The installer takes you through four steps and doesn’t touch your settings or your other addons.
It finds your game on its own and tells you which version you have.

items: Download **Instalar-Alfa.exe** from Alfa’s GitHub page or from La Jauría’s Discord.
Open it. If Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”, click **More info** and then **Run anyway**.
The installer looks for your WoW Forever. If it can’t find it, choose the folder where you installed the game (the one with the `_forever_` folder inside).
If the game is open, close it: the installer waits, downloads the newest version, checks it and installs it.
Enter the game with your character. Done!

bloques.texto: To update, open **Instalar-Alfa.exe** again: it always gets the newest version. If you use the CurseForge app, it also recognizes Alfa and lets you know when there’s a new version.
Install by hand with the zip

items: Download `Alfa-<version>.zip` from CurseForge or from the GitHub releases page.
Close the game.
Unzip it inside `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns`. You should end up with several folders whose names start with `Alfa`.
Enter the game. In the AddOns list on the character screen, check that Alfa is enabled.

bloques.texto: The first time: the welcome

bloques.pie: Each welcome screen is a single decision. You’re in charge.

bloques.texto: When you log in, the wolf howls at the moon and Alfa’s setup greets you: a full, very visual screen that asks how you want to play. Lya introduces herself and keeps you company at every step. It takes about two minutes.
Until you finish it, Alfa’s windows take you back to it. Your bags and combat work normally from the start.
At the end you’ll see a summary of everything you chose and a single button: **Done**.

items.texto: Alfa in 10 languages, even if your game is in another.
Your she-wolf companion introduces herself.
One of the five styles, and Simple or Full Alfa.
“Alfa does it for you”, “Balanced” or “I decide”.
A mosaic: turn each one on with a click.
Whether the pack sees you on the map.
Check everything and press “Done”.

bloques.texto: Want to change something later? Type `/alfa bienvenida` and the summary opens: each step has its own “Change” button. If you like deciding every detail, the usual lists are still there, behind **Fine-tune one by one**.

items.texto: To get started: only Today, Route, Map, Bags and Lya in view, and fewer alerts. Everything else is still there when you look for it.
Every page in view: dungeons, talents, combat, professions, the pack and more.

bloques.texto: If you already used Alfa, you stay on Full. Change it any time in **Settings > Style and sound**, under “How you see Alfa”.
Every time you log in

bloques.pie: After an update, a window tells you what changed.

bloques.texto: The wolf greets you with “Back with the pack!” every time you enter the game (not when you reload the UI). Skip it with a click, [[Esc]], the space bar or [[Enter]], and if a fight starts it goes away on its own.
When Alfa updates, a small window with what’s new appears after the intro: **Keep playing** closes it and **See everything new** tells you the rest.
Rather log in without the intro? Turn it off in **Settings > Style and sound**.
The tour: Alfa in five steps

bloques.titulo: The first time you open Alfa, Lya shows you the window

items.texto: The most useful things right now.
Each one with its pages.
A setting or something in the game.
Lya explains every page.
Right-click: “How can I help?”.

bloques.texto: A green frame points out each part without covering anything. **Next** moves on and **Skip** ends it. Want to see it again? Type `/alfa recorrido` or find it in **Settings > Style and sound**.
Animated announcements

When you arrive by boat or tram, or Lya sniffs out a rare or a treasure, a big announcement appears, like the intro: the wolf with its halo, the name of where you’re arriving or of what showed up and, below, the rest (“Land ho! The pack goes ashore in 0:20”, or the rare’s level and distance). It slides in and leaves on its own, and it never overlaps the zone name or the game’s own banners: it shows before or after. The rare one takes you hunting with a click. If you prefer the old cards, turn it off in **Settings > Style and sound**.

capitulos.lema: All of Alfa in one place: type /alfa.

bloques.texto: Type `/alfa` in chat (or click the Alfa button on the minimap) and the main window opens. Your character is at the top; below is everything Alfa can do, sorted into six sections plus Settings.

bloques.pie: The Alfa window, open on Today.
leyenda: Your character: name, class, level, experience and rest.
Search settings: type what you’re looking for and Alfa takes you to the option.
The six sections: Today, Adventure, Character, World, Trades and Pack.
Settings: style, conveniences, quests and everything else.
Reset page and Reload UI, in case something looks off.

bloques.texto: One Alfa menu

items: **Click** Alfa’s minimap icon, its floating button, its entry in the addon list or the **Alfa** button in the [[Esc]] menu: the window opens on the last page you saw.

**Right-click** any of them: the same menu, with the window’s seven sections and their pages, plus **Ask Lya**, **Arrange your screen**, show or hide the arrow, **Hide Alfa** and **Report a problem**.

bloques.texto: The sections

items.texto: Your day: the next step, what’s urgent and your class.
Route and guides, Dungeons and Encyclopedia.
Talents, Combat, Healing, Bags and Lya.
The map, Gathering, and Landscape and graphics.
Trade and Fishing.
La Jauría: your group, those who share and the clan.
Style and sound, Conveniences, Questing and more.
Find any option by typing its name.

bloques.texto: With **Simple Alfa** you only see Today, Route, Map, Bags and Lya, plus Settings, without its advanced pages (like the ones for guide authors). Everything else keeps working: open it with its command or with “Search settings”.
Five styles

bloques.pie: Settings > Style and sound: your style and the others to choose from.

bloques.texto: Alfa dresses the way you like. **Alfa** is graphite with cut corners and La Jauría’s green; **La Jauría Night**, midnight blue with moonlit silver; **Campfire**, warm charcoal with the orange of embers; **Classic WoW** uses the game’s own frames, buttons and fonts, with gold titles; **Glass** lets the world show through transparent backgrounds, in the accent color you choose. The style can also dress the chat, the minimap and your action bars (in Conveniences). Change it in **Settings > Style and sound** or with `/alfa estilo`.
Every page has its own command: `/alfa bolsas` opens Bags and `/alfa mapa` opens the map. The full list is in the “Shortcuts and commands” chapter.

items: **The “?” next to the title.** Tap it and Lya explains that page, starting with its questions.
**Search settings searches all of Alfa.** Besides options, it finds quests, rares and NPCs: one click opens their page or sets the arrow.
**“What’s this?”** Hold [[Alt]] and hover over any Alfa button or option: it tells you what it’s for.

bloques.texto: Did you know the wolf howls the first time you open the Alfa window each session? It’s a howl from the game itself, so it follows your volume. If you’d rather have silence, turn it off in Style and sound.

capitulos.lema: “What do we do today?”: your next step, what’s urgent and your class.

bloques.texto: Today is Alfa’s front page: the first thing you see when you open the window. It gathers what you should do right now on a single page and puts everything one click away. Only what’s useful shows up: if a part has nothing useful, it stays hidden.

bloques.pie: Today, at a glance.
leyenda: Your next step: what your guide asks, how far it is and how much you’ve done. **Follow** sets the arrow.
Pick up quests: the ones on your route that are close by.
Something else today?: level up, professions, make gold or dungeons.
Alerts: only what’s urgent, with a button to sort it out.

bloques.texto: What you’ll find, top to bottom

items: **Your next step.** Your guide’s step with its goals, how far away it is, how much you’ve done and, at your pace, how long you need to finish it. **Follow** shows the guide and the arrow and closes the window; **See steps** opens the full list.
**Close my quests and Pick up quests.** One click builds the route to turn in what you have ready or to grab the best quests in the zone.
**An hour of hunting.** Not sure what to do? Alfa picks what pays off most nearby: turn in what’s ready, finish your zone’s quests or pick up new ones.
**Your plan.** If you follow one of *My plans*, your current goal is here.

**Alerts.** Worn gear, full bags (with what you can sell and how much you’ll get), abilities to train or a missing buff, each with its own button: “Take me to repair”, “Take me to my trainer”… With Lya in sight, she tells you in her bubble.
**Find nearby.** Flight, inn, repair, bank, mailbox and your trainer: one button points the arrow to the closest one.
**For your class.** The talent to take now and cards made for your class.
**Today in numbers.** Experience per hour, how much you need to level up, today’s gold and your pack.
**Your journal and your alerts.** Today’s session, earlier ones and the reminders you want to get.

bloques.titulo: The four paths of “Something else today?”

items.texto: A guide for your level and zone, with its own quest route.
Level your profession or gather your materials from where you are.
Quests that pay well and materials that sell well.
The dungeon for your level, its quests and how to get there.

bloques.texto: Your play session

items.titulo: How much time do you have?
items.texto: Pick 30 min, 1 h, 2 h or other: Alfa builds the plan (turn-ins, finishing your zone’s quests, a dungeon if it fits, gathering and your guide) and takes you step by step.
How many hours you have left at your pace, how far you got today and which guides and dungeons come next (`/alfa camino`).
Before you go in, it checks your gear, bags, food, water, arrows and reagents, with the arrow to whatever is missing (`/alfa listo`).
It warns you when you run low and what’s worth buying at your level, with the arrow to the vendor.

bloques.texto: If you’re away for a few days, Lya greets you with an “I haven’t seen you in days!” and a button that opens Today so you can pick up right where you left off. And with `/alfa sesion` you can see how today’s session is going, in chat.

partes.lema: Your path: the route, knowledge of the whole game and dungeons.

capitulos.lema: Two clicks and Alfa takes you there.

bloques.texto: The route is the heart of Alfa. You tell it what you want to do and it plans the way: which quests to take, where to go and when to turn them in. An arrow on screen leads you step by step, flights and boats included.
Start with the assistant

bloques.pie: “What do you want to do today?”: five paths.

items: In Today or in **Adventure > Route**, click “What do you want to do?”.
Pick a path: **Level up**, **Professions**, **Make gold**, **Dungeons** or **My own plan**.
On the second click, Alfa suggests the option that suits you best and gets it going.
Alfa’s windows close and your guide stays on screen, with the arrow pointing at your first step.

bloques.texto: Your guide on screen

bloques.pie: The tracker: compact, with only what you’re doing right now.
leyenda: Your guide and how many steps you’ve done.
Find nearby: flight, inn, repair, bank and more.
What’s up now. Click: the arrow; right-click: mark it, skip it or see it in the Encyclopedia.
Where you’re headed.
**See details**: the whole step, with all its goals, in another window.
**Skip** jumps over the step (and for a minute you can **Undo**); **See the next one** lets you peek at what’s coming.

bloques.texto: On arrival

items: The arrow becomes an Alfa plate: on the left, the wolf in its medallion, alert and sniffing when it’s time to search, or howling when you’ve arrived.
At the top it says **YOU MADE IT** (or **SEARCH AROUND HERE**, if what you want is somewhere in the area) and, below, what to do there in plain words.
Your progress shows as a trail of paw prints (“4 of 6”); experience, as a bar with its percentage: “Reach level 30: 20% to go”.
**Next spot**, inside the same plate, takes you to the next point with one click.
If the plate shows your progress (“1 of 10”), it stays while it lasts; if not, it goes away on its own after a few seconds.

bloques.texto: Only quests you can actually do

Before sending you on a quest, Alfa checks your level, class, race, faction, professions and reputation. If a prerequisite quest is missing, it adds it first, in order. Whatever you can’t complete is hidden along with the reason, so you never walk there for nothing. Dungeon quests take you to the entrance.

bloques.titulo: It warns you along the way
items: **Grey quests worth doing.** If a grey quest gives something good or opens another one, your guide tells you.
**Chain warning.** Before you abandon a quest that opens others, it tells you which one you’d lose.
**Dangerous zone.** When you enter a zone with enemies far above your level, a short warning with their levels.

**When your guide runs out.** It tells you whether you finished it or how many steps were left, with “See what’s left”. If your plan runs out of steps, it rebuilds it with a click, and after finishing an “Unlock” guide, Alfa takes you back to the one you were following.

items.texto: How much experience you still need and where it pays best: enemies of your level that also count for your quests. **Take me there** sets the arrow.
Before you get there, Alfa warns you and offers to call the pack.
In a group, if someone is missing a quest you have, a button to share it. Always with your click.

items.titulo: The next guide, on its own
items.texto: When you finish a guide, Alfa suggests the next one for your level.
At the flight master, a paw print marks the destination that brings you closest to your next step. Flying is your click.
In dungeons and in combat your guide goes compact; when you leave, it’s back the way you had it.
All your quests here, the ones you have and the ones you can pick up, in the best order and with the arrow. On the Route page or your guide’s menu.
Pick a destination and Alfa plans the trip with flights, boats, zeppelins, the tram, portals and on foot, leg by leg (`/alfa llevame`).
Grey quests that are no longer worth it, each with “Abandon”. You confirm it.
Its button says which item it is and your progress (“Torch · 2 of 5”) and pulses when you can use it.
The quests before and after, which ones you’ve done and the final reward. From a quest’s menu.
In a group, the map marks what each quest asks for and who has it: “Ana, Beto”.

bloques.texto: Guide library

bloques.pie: The recommended guide for your level and zone, front and center, and all the others by category.

bloques.texto: Close my quests and Pick up quests

**Close my quests** works out the best order to turn in what you already have ready (and finish what’s left), counting flights, boats and your Hearthstone. **Pick up quests** gathers the best ones you can take nearby, without going over your quest log limit. You’ll find both in Today, in Route and in your guide.
When turning in

items: **Turn-in run.** With two or more quests ready, your guide offers it: Alfa orders them along the shortest path and the arrow takes you one by one (“Turn-in 2 of 4”).
**Hearthstone time.** If almost everything you’ll turn in is in your hearthstone’s town and you’re far away, Lya suggests using it. You press the “Use the stone” button yourself.

**The best reward.** When turning in, a paw print marks the reward that suits you best (or the most valuable one) and below it says “Alfa recommends”. It only marks it: the choice is yours, unless you turn on “Take the best reward”.

bloques.texto: When you complete a quest, your chat says “[Quest] is ready to turn in” and, when you hand it in, “Quest complete!”. If you turn on **Tell your group** (in Your extras in the setup), your group sees it too; it comes off so nobody’s chat gets flooded.
My plans: your own goals

bloques.pie: A plan is a list of goals in whatever order you like.

bloques.texto: Build a list of goals: get an item, save up gold, level a profession, go somewhere, do a quest, reach a level or write a free note. Goals check themselves off when you complete them, and the arrow takes you to the next one.
Out of ideas? Start from a template: *My first mount*, *Gold for the mount*, *Get ready for the dungeon* or *Level cooking and fishing together*.
Find nearby

bloques.pie: The closest places, by travel time.

bloques.texto: The button with the location pin, next to your guide (and also in Today and on the map), tells you what’s closest by travel time: flight master, innkeeper, repair, bank, mailbox, auction house, your trainer, profession trainers, vendors and more.
One click sets the arrow and the route. Also with `/alfa cerca`.
In **Settings > Questing** you decide whether Alfa accepts and turns in only your route’s quests or all of them. Route takes you there with one button.

capitulos.lema: The whole game, even what you don’t have.

bloques.texto: The Encyclopedia is the game’s wiki inside Alfa: every item, mount, pet, NPC, quest, zone and rare, with where to get it and how to get there. Open it in **Adventure > Encyclopedia** or with `/alfa enciclopedia`.

bloques.pie: Search, filter and open its page: who drops it, who sells it and which quest gives it.

items: Type the name of what you’re looking for (in English or Spanish) or its number, like `#12345`.
Pick the type (items, mounts, companions, NPCs, quests, zones or rares) and narrow it down with the filters: quality, level, slot or “I can use”.
Open its page. What’s best for you comes first; then each source with its details.
Click **Guide me** and Alfa plans the way there, with the arrow.

items.texto: The route to the best source.
What you need first: a level, a prerequisite quest, a key…
Where it is, on Alfa’s map.
Turn it into a goal in your plan.

bloques.texto: Mounts and pets

bloques.pie: Every mount and pet, with how to get it, its level, its faction and whether you already have it.

bloques.texto: Filter by the ones you can get, the ones you already have or are missing, the source and the faction. The **My first mount** guide tells you how much riding training costs, which mount is the cheapest for your race, how much gold you still need and who to go to.
The Encyclopedia also has a guide to Forever’s **Legacy points**: what they are, how to earn them and what they’re for. And each zone’s page includes what Lya tells about it.

capitulos.lema: The right one for you, what to bring and how to get there.

bloques.texto: Dungeons tells you which dungeon fits your level and gets you ready in one click: it picks up the quests worth bringing and points the arrow at the entrance. Open it in **Adventure > Dungeons** or with `/alfa mazmorras`.

bloques.pie: “For your level now” front and center and, below, every dungeon by level range.

items: Open Dungeons: the recommended one for your level is at the top.
Press **Get me ready** (or “Take me to the entrance”).
Alfa picks up only the quests you can already take and tells you what the others still need.
Follow the arrow to the entrance. Once inside, a prompt takes you to the bosses.

items.texto: What to do now, what its quests are worth and its requirements.
Each boss with tips for your role, its loot and its quests.
By boss, with “What I can use”, the drop chance and whether you have it.
To pick up, in your log, not yet and already done.
Before you go in, plus the game’s boss alerts.
Dungeons done, bosses defeated and loot: `/alfa mazmorras progreso`.

bloques.texto: **The dungeon, live.** When you target a boss, a small card appears at the top of the screen with its name, your job for your role (tank, healer or damage) and your quests there, checked off. It doesn’t catch clicks and goes away by itself when the fight ends. And before you go in, `/alfa listo` checks you carry what you need.
**Story mode** comes turned on: bosses you haven’t beaten yet stay undiscovered, with no spoilers. You can still view their tips on purpose. Change it in **Settings > Discovery**.

When you reach a zone with a dungeon for your level, I tell you who from the pack is nearby and at your level, so you can invite them. When you go in I give you a little tip with “See the dungeon”, and when you come out I tell you how long it took, how many times you fell and the best thing you got.

partes.lema: Your talents, your combat, your bags… and your she-wolf.

capitulos.lema: What to take now and why, in one click.

bloques.texto: Talents tells you which talent to take now, explains why and applies it in one click. You choose your build in two clicks. Open it in **Character > Talents** or with `/alfa talentos`.

bloques.pie: Your path: what you want to do and how you play. Alfa puts together the build that fits you.

items: In **Your path**, choose what you want: **Solo leveling**, **Dungeons**, **Tank** or **PvP**.
Choose how you play: **Steady**, **Balanced** or **Risky**, and your talent tree if there’s more than one.
The talent to take shows up big at the top, with its why. Press **Apply**.
When you level up, a prompt tells you the next one, ready to apply.

items.texto: Your points with the plan on top: what’s done in green and what’s next with a ring.
The talents coming up, with their level and their why.
Which stats to look for and the best gear for your level in each slot.
Copy your build as a code and pass it to anyone you like.

bloques.texto: Alfa never removes talents, and it never applies anything in combat or while the game’s talent window is open. If your points are going another way, it tells you and offers to follow the build for the tree you’re already on.
At each level, Alfa also tells you about the new spells you can learn, from which trainer and how much they cost, and about old ranks still on your bars: **Update my bars** swaps them.

capitulos.lema: It shows you; you press.

bloques.texto: Combat lends you a hand in fights without deciding for you: it shows which ability is worth using now, alerts you when something becomes usable and highlights the enemies your quests need. Nothing here presses, casts or targets for you. Open it in **Character > Combat** or with `/alfa combate`.

bloques.pie: The rotation helper (reference drawing).
leyenda: The big icon is the ability worth using now.
The small ones are the ones that come next.
A dark sweep shows the running cooldown.
The border pulses when the game makes that ability glow. “Area” shows up with three or more enemies.
Below, a short line tells you why.

bloques.texto: The rotation helper knows all **27 specializations** of the 9 classes and grows with you: it only suggests what you’ve already learned, at your highest rank. The first time, a note explains how to read it. The icon moves wherever you want, can now be much bigger and shows your bar’s key on top, nice and clear.

items.texto: Overpower, Revenge, Execute, Counterattack… right when they can be used.
The enemies you need, marked on their nameplate.
Your group’s damage, when your game includes the meter (`/alfa dps`).
When your target casts something you can interrupt, it tells you with your ability, its key and whether it’s ready (`/alfa combate corte` tests it).
A small bar that warns you before you pull the enemy off the tank or, if you tank, before you lose it.
When it ends: how long it lasted, your damage and healing per second and what hit you hardest. The last one, with `/alfa combate pelea`.
A discreet bar with whatever takes 30 seconds or more to come back; each one leaves on its own when it’s ready.

bloques.texto: When you’re solo, Combat stays out of the way: the interrupt alert’s sound and the fight summary show in a group, in instances or in long fights. If you always want them, the Combat page has **Also when solo** and **Solo, fights of at least**.

All of this only shows: nothing takes the mouse in combat and nothing casts for you. Healers start with the rotation helper off (the welcome decides based on your role); each helper is turned on or off in Combat.

capitulos.lema: Hover, click, heal.

bloques.texto: Healing adds party and raid frames made for click healing: hover over a teammate, click and cast the spell you chose. The same click targets them, their debuffs and missing buff show at a glance, and it tells you which click fixes them. Any priest, druid, paladin or shaman uses it with no setup; other classes use it for their buffs, a bandage and targeting.

bloques.pie: The Healing page: “Your clicks” at the top, your frames and the presets.

bloques.texto: No group? Your frames appear when you join one. Meanwhile, the page lets you see them with **See how they look**.
Your clicks

The first thing on the page is **Your clicks**: a row for each of the most used clicks (left, right, middle and the Shift and Ctrl ones). Open its list and choose: your heals, **Remove debuffs**, your buffs, **Revive**, other spells from your spellbook, **Use a bandage**, **Target** or the **Player menu**. Not sure what to pick? The **Presets** suggest some clicks for your class; then change whatever you like.

items: **Choose your clicks.** A preset for your class and “Heal and target”; if you heal, the left click can stay just for targeting.
**Place your frames.** With sample frames you drag around: width, height, columns and which way they grow.
**Test your clicks.** Click a sample frame (with or without Shift, Ctrl or Alt) and Alfa tells you what it would cast, without casting anything.

bloques.pie: Twelve clicks for twelve actions: three mouse buttons, with or without Shift, Ctrl or Alt. (Example)

bloques.texto: Heal and target

It comes on: every click that heals on your frames also makes that teammate your target. That way you keep going with them without looking for them again: a buff, another heal or removing a curse from your bar. The bandage works the same. If you’d rather your target didn’t change, turn off **Heal and target** on the Healing page.

bloques.titulo: Cleanse with one click, step by step
items: In **Your clicks**, pick one for **Remove debuffs** (for example, Shift + left click). If your class removes something and no click does it, the page and your chat let you know.
In a fight, the frame of anyone with something **you** can remove turns the color of the debuff: magic, curse, poison or disease, with its icon at the top right.
Hover over that frame: the tooltip tells you what they have and which click removes it, such as “Poison: remove it with Shift + left click”.
Make that click and you’re done: the color and the icon go away on their own.

bloques.titulo: The little blue dot: they’re missing your buff
items: Out of combat, which is when buffs get handed out, a **blue dot** at the bottom right of a frame means that teammate is missing your class’s buff.
Hover over it: it tells you which one is missing and which click gives it.
Make the click. Once they have it, the dot goes out; group buffs count too.
Health in the class color, and incoming heals in a light green band.
A red line if someone has the enemy’s aggro.
The color and icon of the debuff **you** can remove, and the blue dot for the missing buff.
Faded if out of range; gray if dead, a ghost or disconnected.

items.texto: The tank’s frame pulses red when they have less than 40% health left.
Above your frames, the mana of your group’s healers. It stands out after each fight, so you know whether it’s worth waiting.
With “In a raid, one group per column”, each group goes in its own column, like in the raid window.
Any class can put “Use a bandage” on a click: Alfa uses the best one in your bags.

bloques.texto: Forgot what the blue dot was or how to remove a poison? Ask me with `/alfa ayuda`: I’ll explain it and take you to “Your clicks”.
The frames rearrange themselves even in combat, but changing what your clicks do has to happen out of combat: the game requires it. With **Move frames** you can put them wherever you like.

capitulos.lema: Your bags, your bank and all your characters.

bloques.texto: Bags puts all your bags in a single Alfa window that opens with the usual [[B]] and when you visit a vendor, the mailbox or the bank. It also shows your bank from anywhere and what your other characters carry.

bloques.pie: The Bags page: your bank, more space and what to sell or keep.

items.texto: Every slot in its place, with the keyring at the end.
Gear, consumables, quest items, crafting, junk…
Each bag in its own block, with how many slots it has left.

bloques.texto: Search and sort
Search by name, type, quality (“green”, “blue”, “purple”) or item level (“20”, “>20”, “20-30”): matches light up and everything else fades. **Sort** tidies everything up in one click.

items: Its item level and a border in its quality color.
A coin on junk and a sparkle on new items.
A green arrow if it’s an upgrade for you.
**Quest items glow** with a golden border and a “!”; the “!” is filled in if the item starts a quest you don’t have yet.

bloques.texto: The bank

At a banker, your bank opens in the same kind of window; away from one, you see the last snapshot Alfa took. **Quick deposit** stores, in one click, whatever you already keep in the bank, all your materials or a whole category. The bank bar shows you the cost of the next slot.

items.texto: How much you’ve earned since you logged in and your rate per hour, at the bottom of your bags and on their page.
With 2 free slots or fewer, Alfa tells you what’s best to drop first, with “Sell” if you have a vendor open.
If you get something better than what you’re wearing, **Put it on** equips it with one click (out of combat).
What’s more useful in the bank or on another of your characters, with **To the bank** if a banker is nearby.
Save what you’re wearing under a name (healing, damage, fishing…) and put it on with one click, out of combat. On the Bags page or with `/alfa bolsas conjunto`.
In each piece’s tooltip, what you gain and what you lose against what you’re wearing: “+5 Strength · −3 Stamina”.
Search the bags, banks and gear of all your characters, with filters for type, quality and character.
A button in your bags: at the vendor, it sells your junk; at the banker, it stores your materials. Another click stops it.

bloques.texto: The bags got a thorough check-up: special bags (quivers, ammo, soul and herb bags) no longer count as free space, ammo and shards stay with you, the bank is read again when it changes, and items with a suffix (“of the Bear”) show up when you search.
When your bags fill up, Alfa tells you what to sell and what to keep, using Trade’s prices: **Mark as junk**, **Take me to a vendor** and, with the vendor open, **Sell the junk**.

capitulos.lema: Your she-wolf companion.

bloques.texto: Lya is a little black she-wolf who keeps you company on screen: she gives you short tips, cheers you on and tells you stories about the world. She’s named after Lya, toxic3000’s dog: noble, loyal and always by her family’s side, the chubby, pampered darling of the house. Alfa remembers her that way, as the she-wolf who looks after the pack and never leaves anyone behind.

items: quieta1
Keeps you company
atenta1
Perks up
sentada1
Sits
pedir2
Begs for a sausage
correr3
Runs
cola2
Chases her tail
estirarse2
Stretches
saltar2
Jumps
aullar2
Howls
dormir2
Sleeps

bloques.texto: I love chatting about the zone we’re in, your race and your professions. And if you see me sitting with my little bone… it means I’m hungry. Will you give me a sausage?

items: **She keeps you company.** She breathes, wags her tail, runs, stretches, howls when you level up and curls up to sleep if you step away for a while. In combat she stays still and faint, so she won’t distract you.

**She tells you the alerts.** Worn gear, full bags, abilities to train, quests ready to turn in and Alfa’s notices, in her bubble and with their button. If she’s hidden or you’re in combat, they show up as usual.
**She tells you stories.** She keeps the story of every quest you take, even if you accept it without reading, and when you turn it in she offers you the ending.
**She knows it all.** Warcraft lore, fun facts about every zone in Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, about your race, your class and your professions, and advice from a friend.

bloques.pie: Lya talks in her speech bubble, without getting in the way, when things are calm.

items.texto: Opens “Ask Lya” (below).
For when you need to focus.

items.titulo: Tell me something about this place · Tell me something
items.texto: A fact about your zone, lore, tips and things about your race.
Opens the Stories window.
Many, few or important only; normal, large or extra large text. Each click moves to the next.
Keep her in place, open her page or hide her; bring her back with `/alfa lya`.

bloques.pie: The Stories window gathers what you were told in each quest, by zone and with a search box (`/alfa historias`).

bloques.texto: Ask Lya
Right-click Lya and choose **How can I help?**, type `/alfa ayuda` or use her key. Lya explains every part of Alfa in her own words and takes you there with **Take me there**.

items: Common questions, what would help you right now (full bags, broken gear, quests to turn in) and every page of Alfa, with a search box.
At the top, the last things she told you, with their buttons, in case her bubble left before you read it (`/alfa lya historial`: the 20 most recent).
When Alfa brings something new, Lya introduces it once. And each page’s “?” takes you straight to its questions.

bloques.texto: Your hunting day

items: Lya counts each day’s quests, levels, gold, rares and time. Ask her with `/alfa lya dia`, and for your week with `/alfa lya semana`.
When you come back another day she tells you how it went last time, and lets you know if you break your record for quests in a day.
She celebrates with you: a little hop when you turn in a quest and cheers every 5 in a day. If you like, a short howl with every quest too (on her page, off by default).
In a group she howls when someone levels up, with **Congratulate in group** to send your congratulations in one click.

items.texto: If you keep dying she comforts you and offers help; if you level fast, she celebrates.
Now and then she asks you for one (“Give her a sausage”) and keeps count.
A short tip when you go in and, when you come out, how it went.
At the top of a rank, she tells you that you can learn the next one and where your trainer is.
When you log out she reminds you of the quests that are ready, or says goodbye with your hunting day.
Her bubble on a single line; hover over it to read it in full.
She tells you whether to run back to your body or use the spirit healer, with the numbers, and sets the arrow.
Lines for the time of day, the game’s holidays and the zone you’re in.
When you learn a spell: what it’s for and when to use it.
In dungeons and in combat she gets tiny, goes quiet and stays out of the way; when you leave, she’s back.
If your teammates have Alfa, their Lyas and yours greet each other when you group up and chat now and then.
Every quest you accept, summed up in two lines: what to do and a comment of hers.
She greets your pet by name and, if you’re a hunter, tells you when it’s hungry or sad.
Three little challenges every week, with their progress on her page. Each one completed earns her a sausage.
Every year she celebrates the day she met your character, and Alfa’s too, on November 16.
In “Ask Lya” she explains Heal and target, how to remove a poison and the blue dot.

bloques.texto: Your story and what Lya learns
On her page (**Character > Lya** or `/alfa lya historia`), **Your story** is the diary of your big steps: your levels, your first dungeon, your mount, your first rare and your best day.

**Lya learns:** if you close the same kind of tip three times, she asks whether you don’t want it anymore. What you ask her to keep quiet goes to “Tips you muted”, and you bring it back whenever you like with **Bring back**.

Give Lya a click whenever you want a tip. You can drag her anywhere you like and, with “Lock position”, she stays put. In the game’s key bindings, Alfa section, “What Lya offers” does what her first button does (“Take me there”, “Turn them all in”…) without touching the mouse.

partes.lema: The map, resources and how the world looks.

capitulos.lema: All of Azeroth on one map, with the M key.

bloques.texto: Alfa’s map puts the whole world on one zoomable map: the real terrain, flight points, entrances and exits, your markers and your group. It opens with the usual [[M]] (or with `/alfa mapa`) and centers on your zone.

e.zoom: Zoom in, zoom out and center on you

bloques.pie: The map window and its buttons (reference drawing).

items.texto: Zooms in or out where the cursor is.
Moves the map; let go quickly and it glides a bit before stopping.
Zooms in.
Places a marker there (Shift-click works too).
The arrow and the route to that point, without saving anything.
Opens and closes the map.
Zoom in and you see the minimap’s ground: mountains, rivers and roads. In the gear menu, choose “Terrain” or “Classic”.
Green for the ones you know; amber with a “?” for the ones you’re missing. Hover to see where you can fly from there.
Dungeons, zone exits with their destination, boats, zeppelins, the tram and portals.
Mining, herbs, fishing and treasures as you zoom into a zone; faded if your skill isn’t high enough.
Your group, in their class colors; those who share their location, with a small paw print.
One click leaves only the essentials: you, your group, your markers and your guide.

bloques.texto: Your markers

items: Right-click on Alfa’s map (on the game’s map, Shift-right-click).
Give it a name and choose one of 13 icons and 10 colors. Press **Save**.
Click its pin to change it, share it with your group, delete it or **Follow** it: the arrow and the route take you there.

bloques.texto: Your markers show up on Alfa’s map, on the game’s map and on the minimap. The full list is under the paw print button, and on the **World** page along with the **Alfa layers** and clean mode.

items: Your spot stands out: your arrow has a ring and a soft pulse, so you find yourself instantly.
The route line to your destination, pulsing so you see it, with the distance and how much is left.
On a gryphon, the line of your flight: where you are, where you land and the time left.
A one-piece map: zooming in shows no stitched-together tiles.
Wolf notes, farming spots, the pack’s dens and the mark of a call also show up here (chapter “La Jauría”).

items.texto: Each dock with its countdown (“1:20”); hover over it to see where it goes and when it leaves.
Elites and dangerous rares in your zone: red if 3+ levels above you, amber if not.
Corners of your zone you haven’t explored yet, and their experience.
Flight masters in your zone you don’t have yet; one click sets the arrow.
On the World page, how much of each zone you’ve explored.

bloques.texto: Inside a dungeon, [[M]] opens the game’s map. From Alfa’s map, “Go to the game’s map” opens the game’s map where you are, and on the game’s map the “Alfa’s map” button takes you back.

capitulos.lema: Ore, herbs, fish and treasures, with a route.

bloques.texto: Gathering shows you the mining nodes, herbs, fishing pools and treasures of WoW Forever on the map and the minimap, and builds farming routes in your zone. It comes with about 25,000 spots out of the box and learns the ones you discover.

bloques.pie: Build a route with what your skill can reach, and the arrow takes you from stop to stop.

items: Open **World > Gathering** (`/alfa recoleccion`).
Choose what to gather: the type (mining, herbs, fishing or treasures) and, if you like, a specific resource.
Press **Create route**: Alfa joins the spots into a short loop and draws it on the map.
Press **Guide me**: the arrow goes to the closest stop and moves on to the next when you arrive or gather.
Each spot has its type’s color: copper for mining, green for herbs, blue for fishing and gold for treasures.
What your skill can’t reach yet shows up gray and faded.
On hover: the required skill, how many times you’ve gathered it and when you last did.
The history counts what you gather per session, per hour and per zone.

bloques.texto: No gathering profession yet? Gathering takes you to a trainer so you can learn one.

capitulos.lema: Make the world look gorgeous, without the hassle.

bloques.texto: Landscape and graphics explains the game’s graphics settings in plain words (even the ones the menu hides), comes with presets and undoes changes in one click. Open it in **World > Landscape and graphics** or with `/alfa paisaje`.

bloques.pie: Six tabs (Quality, Environment, Camera, Interface, Filters and Advanced), with a search box.

items.texto: The lightest, to raise your frames per second.
Balanced: looks good on almost any computer.
More view distance, fine shadows and water with reflections.
Everything at the safe maximum. Needs a strong graphics card.
Alfa’s signature: more grass, more horizon, light fog and sunbeams.
Brings back what you had before the last preset.

items: **Installing it changes nothing**: it only reads. Alfa doesn’t touch a setting until you ask.
Optional **screen filters**: tint, vignette, grain and cinema bars, which never cover the interface.
Nothing is touched in combat: whatever you ask for waits until the fight is over.
If the game limits a value, the row tells you: “You asked for 2.6; the game set it to 2.”

partes.lema: Fish at your own pace and make gold wisely.

capitulos.lema: One key for everything.

bloques.texto: Fishing completely re-engineers fishing: a mode where a single key equips your pole, applies the lure, casts and loots. It also brings a bar, a catch journal, goals, 22 achievements, a 1 to 300 guide and cooking by the water.

e.cada: Each press does the next step

bloques.pie: Always with your key, and out of combat.

items: Open fishing mode: with the button on its page, with `/alfa pesca` or simply by equipping a fishing pole.
Press [[Space]]: Alfa equips your best pole and your fishing gear.
Press it again: it applies the best lure. Once more: it casts.
When the bobber splashes, press [[Space]] to loot.
When you close the mode, your normal gear comes back. If you take off the pole and put your weapons on yourself, the mode closes on its own.

items.texto: The next step. You can change the key: keyboard, mouse buttons or the wheel.
Jump, as always.
Drop the cast and cast again.
When you move, your key goes back to what it normally does.

bloques.pie: The fishing bar: your skill and what your key will do.
The Fishing page: journal, statistics, guide, cooking, goals and achievements.

items.texto: Everything you can catch in Forever and what you’ve already caught, with masteries.
Casts, catches and value, per session and all-time.
Where to fish for your skill, trainers, vendors and the Stranglethorn Fishing Extravaganza.
Set yourself goals and unlock 22 achievements of its own. And cook your catch by the water.

capitulos.lema: Vendor it, auction it or craft it?

bloques.texto: Trade answers a single question for every item: should I sell it to a vendor, auction it or turn it into something worth more? At the auction house it only informs: it never buys, sells or posts anything for you. And at the mailbox it warns you about letters about to expire.

bloques.pie: The Trade page: what to do with what you carry, and auction house prices.

items: Go to the auction house: Alfa’s bar appears below its window.
Press **Scan with Alfa**. It saves the lowest price of every item (you have to wait 15 minutes between scans).
Hover over any item: two lines tell you its price and the best thing you can do with it.
In **Trades > Trade** you see how much you earn if you follow the advice, and what’s worth vendoring, auctioning, crafting or keeping.

bloques.pie: Alfa’s two lines in an item’s tooltip (example).

items: It learns from what you look up by hand at the auction house and from what things cost at vendors.
It reads your recipes and works out whether crafting pays off; disenchanting too, if you or one of your characters can.
It recommends whatever earns the most gold, as long as it beats vendoring by at least 10%; if nothing earns gold, it tells you to keep the item.
Prices older than 60 days are forgotten on their own.

bloques.texto: Bags uses this advice: when your bags fill up, it tells you what to sell and how much you’ll get.
Your professions, 1 to 300

The Trade page lists your professions with their skill. A click (or `/alfa comercio oficios`) opens each one’s guide: your next step, each stretch with its recipe and materials, what’s left from here to 300 and, when it’s time, **Take me to the trainer**.

**What to craft for the most profit.** In “Your recipes that make a profit”, each recipe with what its result is worth minus what its materials cost, how many times you can already make it with what’s in your bags and bank, and how much you’d earn. The ones you can make now come first. It only informs: crafting and selling are your click.

items.texto: For a recipe or a goal: what you’re missing, how much you have in bags and bank and where to get it. It checks itself off as you gather.
When you list something at the auction house, the suggested price and its price history. Posting is still your click.

bloques.texto: The mailbox: Take all

items: The game already has its own **Open All** at the mailbox, so Alfa doesn’t add a bar of its own.

When you open the mailbox, Alfa warns you if a letter with items expires in less than 3 days. That alert has **Take all**: it takes the money and items from your letters, one by one, and at the end tells you what you received.
Cash-on-delivery letters and letters from a GM are left for you to open yourself.
It stops if you close the mailbox, enter combat or your bags fill up (it keeps taking the money).

capitulos.lema: Your group on the map, with permission, and the clan one click away.

bloques.texto: La Jauría is your pack’s page: your party or raid, and the players who use Alfa and agreed to let the pack see them on the map. Open it in **Pack** or with `/alfa manada`.

bloques.pie: What’s up now, the pack in sight and the clan.

bloques.texto: Sharing your location is your call

Out of the box, nothing is shared. In the welcome you choose “Not for now” or “Yes, let the pack see me”, and you can change it later on this page whenever you like, with “Let the pack see my character on the map”. If you share, only your character’s location in the game is sent. Your group is always visible, just like in the game.
Your location travels over a hidden game channel that someone with another addon could read: share it only if you’re comfortable with that. Nothing is sent inside dungeons and raids.

items: One card per person: their name in their class color, level, zone, distance and how long ago they were last heard from.
**Follow** points the arrow at that person and doesn’t let go, even if they change zones or when you catch up: if they keep walking, it takes you to them again until you let go.
**Invite** adds them to your group.
On the map, your group shows up in their class colors, and those who share, with a small paw print. Their tooltip says which den they’re in.

bloques.texto: La Jauría badges

items.texto: A gold wolf next to the name.
A green wolf next to the name.

bloques.texto: The badge glows on the edge of the portrait (yours, your target’s and your focus’s), on the player’s tooltip, on this page and as a ring on the map. At max level it gains a star and, on yours, a hunter’s mark once you’ve seen 100 rares. It’s only visual: it gives no advantage, and toxic3000 keeps the list, with each person’s permission.
Invite to guild or community

Right-click someone’s portrait, their name in chat, your party or raid, or a community’s list, and choose **Invite to guild or community**. Only the places where you really can invite show up. To your guild, the invitation goes out with one click. For a community, the game asks you to use its own window: Alfa leaves the name ready to copy ([[Ctrl]]+[[C]]) and the **Open Guild & Communities** button; there you press “Invite Member” and paste it.
Dens

When a zone fills up, the game splits it into layers: the same place with other people, other rares and other ore. Alfa names each one (Fang Den, Ember Den…) and in the **Dens** section of this page tells you which one you’re in and where the pack in your zone is. Your den also shows in your on-screen guide.

items: **Ask to enter.** One click (or right-click on the wolf) and Alfa knocks on the door of someone with an open den: they invite you to their group, you accept, the game moves you to their den and Alfa reminds you to leave the group.
**Open my den** (off by default). If someone from the pack asks to enter, Alfa invites them to your group, out of combat.
**Pack rares.** When a wolf finds a rare or a treasure in your zone, you get a notice with their den: “Go hunt” if it’s yours, “Ask to enter” if it’s another.

**Call the pack.** An elite or a really tough rare? Ask for help (or `/alfa manada llamar`): the wolves in your zone get your location, press “On my way!” and you’re told who’s coming. Your call shows on their map for 3 minutes.

items.texto: In a group, when you target an unmarked rare, give it the skull with one click.
If a wolf in your zone has your quest, their card says so and Lya suggests inviting them. Only which quests you have is shared.

When you log in, Lya tells you who from your guild is online and where. And when you see a pack wolf nearby who also uses Alfa (Toxic, the founder, included), a short announcement tells you so you can say hi. Turn it off with **A wolf from La Jauría is nearby**.
Alfa remembers when each rare went down: its tooltip says how long ago it was hunted and whether it could be back.
Suggest what, the day and the time. Your guild gets it with “I’m in” or “Can’t go”; Lya reminds you 15 minutes before.
Near a dungeon for your level, Lya tells you who from the pack is at your level, with a button to invite them.
Type and press “Note here”: it stays on your map where you are. One click and the arrow takes you there. You can share them with your guild.
If your layer fills up with hunters, Lya offers to move you to the layer of a wolf with an open den (`/alfa plano`).
Ask your guild who has an item; each person decides whether to answer.
Lya celebrates when a wolf hits 60, gets their first mount or hunts down a rare. Sharing yours is optional.
What the clan did this week, no rankings: everything counts.
Post who’s looking for a group, for what (dungeon, quest or farming) and at what level. It reaches the wolves in your guild, with “Whisper” and “Invite”; it clears itself after an hour.
Adopt a wolf 10 levels below you. If they accept, you see their level, zone and quest (only you) and it tells you if they get stuck.
If something you picked up is useful to another online wolf, “Give it to them” opens the trade or gets their name ready in the mailbox.
“Spot here” marks a good farming place in gold. With “Share my spots”, your guild sees them too.
Live: which dens the pack is in for each zone and how many wolves are in each one.
The next seven days, each with its events by the hour.

bloques.texto: Almost everything in the pack needs you to share your trail; meetups and notes don’t. Each thing has its own switch in the settings, at the end of this page, and whatever you switch off no longer takes up room.
The clan
At the bottom of the page is La Jauría, the clan: its motto, what it offers, the Discord link to copy and **I want to join**, to ask for your place in the pack.

items.texto: Takes you to someone in your group or who shares.
Stops following.
Starts or stops sharing your location.
Ask the wolves in your zone for help.
Move to the layer of a wolf with an open den.
What’s being sent and received right now.
Suggest an outing to the pack (what, day and time).
Leave a note on your map where you are.
Mark a farming spot where you are.
Post your note on the pack board.

capitulos.lema: Change anything, lose nothing.

bloques.texto: **Settings** (at the top right of the window) is home to everything you can change: the style, conveniences, quests, the map and more. The quickest way in is the search box: type what you want to change in “Search settings” and Alfa takes you to the option.

items.texto: The five styles, Simple or Full Alfa, the howl, the wolf at login, the announcements, easier reading, the clean screen, arranging your screen, your shortcuts, your profiles, your backups, “Check Alfa”, “Report” and what’s new.
Small improvements to the game, all in one place (next chapter).
Accept and turn in on its own, all quests or only your route’s.
The map, dungeons and story mode.
How your on-screen guide looks and behaves.
The story of Alfa and La Jauría, the Discord link to copy, the version and the credits.

bloques.pie: Settings > Questing: each option explained in one line.

bloques.texto: At the bottom left, **Reset page** puts the settings of the page you’re viewing back the way they came.
Easier reading, clean screen and your shortcuts

items: **Bigger text.** All of Alfa’s text a bit larger, in every window.
**Colour-blind friendly colours.** Good things in blue, warnings in yellow and danger in orange; debuffs, in colors you can tell apart without red and green.
**“What’s this?”.** With [[Alt]] held down (or the key you choose), hover over anything in Alfa and it tells you what it’s for. **Help mode** keeps it on without holding the key.
**Clean screen.** One key leaves only Alfa, your guide and Lya in view; you choose what hides (chat, minimap, bars, portraits…). Press it again to bring everything back (`/alfa limpia`).
**Your shortcuts.** All of Alfa’s keys in a single window: click and press the new key (`/alfa teclas`).

bloques.texto: Arrange your screen

items: In **Settings > Style and sound**, under “Arrange your screen”, press **Arrange** (or type `/alfa acomodar`).

The game dims a little and every Alfa thing in view gets a green frame with its name: Lya, your guide, the arrow, the alerts, fishing and the Combat and Healing frames. A thin cross marks the center of the screen.
Drag each one wherever you like. Right-click one to put it back in its usual place.
Press **Done** or [[Esc]] to finish. If a fight starts, it ends on its own.

bloques.texto: Only what’s in view shows up: to move your guide or the fishing bar, open them before you start.
Your profiles

items: In **Settings > Style and sound > Your profiles**, save your setup under a name and go back to it with a click.
**Export** gives you your settings as text to back them up or pass to a friend; **Import** pastes one and applies it.
That text only carries settings: Alfa never runs anything you paste.

bloques.texto: Backups and “Check Alfa”

items: **Backups.** Alfa saves your settings and profiles every week and before each big change (the last 3). In **Settings > Style and sound > Backups** you go back to one with a click; what you have now is kept as the “Before restoring” profile.
If your settings come up empty when you log in, Alfa tells you and offers the latest backup.
**Caught errors.** Alfa notes its own errors, without your name or realm, so you can copy or clear them. “Report” already includes them.
**Check Alfa** (`/alfa diagnostico`) finds clashes with other addons and offers to turn off only the part of Alfa that clashes. The other addon is never touched.

bloques.texto: When you update, your settings stay as you left them. If a version moves them somewhere else, Alfa moves them over for you, just once, without losing anything.

capitulos.lema: Little things that make the game more comfortable.

bloques.texto: Conveniences gathers quality-of-life improvements: each group has its own switch, with its options inside. Open it in **Settings > Conveniences** or with `/alfa comodidades`.

bloques.pie: At the top, how many you have turned on; below, each group with its switch.

bloques.texto: Not sure where to start? Press **Turn on the recommended ones**: class colors, a better tooltip, the dressing room, the flight’s next stop and no error speech.

items.texto: The next stop on flights with layovers, and how long is left.
On the **Minimap and coordinates** tab: square, with addon buttons hidden until you hover. Alfa’s own button always stays in view.
Dresses those parts of the game in your style; turn it off and everything goes back to how it was.
Class colors on your frame and your target’s, and a warning if a form’s bar is empty.
Who someone is targeting, their guild rank and showing it only with Shift.
Buttons to remove pieces, and animation control.
Zoom the camera out a bit further.
Error speech, dialogue, pets, emotes and your own list.

items.a: No. Alfa backs you up and you decide: the welcome asks what you want it to do on its own, and in combat it never presses, casts or targets for you. Healing, fishing, applying talents and using items always take your key or your click.

items.q: Can I have Alfa in a different language from my game?
items.a: Yes. Alfa comes in 10 languages and you can pick any of them, even if your game is in another: type `/alfa bienvenida`, press “Change” on Language and choose. Alfa reloads the interface and stays in your language.

items.q: Who sees me on the map?
items.a: Your group, as always. Other players who use Alfa only see you if you agreed to share your location, and all they see is your character’s location in the game. You can stop sharing whenever you like in La Jauría.

items.q: How do I turn off the wolf intro at login?
items.a: In **Settings > Style and sound**, turn off “The wolf greets you when you log in”. You can turn off the howl right there too.

items.q: Lya talks a lot. How do I calm her down?
items.a: Right-click on her: **Mute for 1 hour**, or switch her tips to “few” or “important only”. If you close the same tip three times, she’ll ask you herself whether you don’t want it anymore. You can also hide her and bring her back with `/alfa lya`.

items.q: How do I know what a page is for?
items.a: Tap the “?” next to its title, or type `/alfa ayuda`: Lya explains it and takes you there with **Take me there**. To see the window tour again, `/alfa recorrido`.

items.q: [[M]] opens the game’s map, not Alfa’s.
items.a: Inside dungeons that’s on purpose: there, [[M]] opens the game’s map. Outside them, check on the **World** page that “Open Alfa’s map with the map key” is turned on.

items.q: Do I lose my settings when I update?
items.a: No. Alfa keeps everything, and if a version moves something, it migrates it by itself, just once. It also backs up your settings every week (**Settings > Style and sound > Backups**).
If you chose **Simple Alfa**, you only see the essentials. Switch to Full in **Settings > Style and sound** (“How you see Alfa”), or open any page with its command or the search box.

items.q: Why does Alfa wait for the fight to end for some things?
items.a: Because the game doesn’t let an addon change certain things in combat. Alfa gets them ready and does them as soon as the fight is over.

items.q: When I heal with a click, my target changes.
items.a: That’s **Heal and target**: the teammate you heal stays targeted so you can follow up with a buff or a cleanse. If you don’t want it, turn it off on the **Healing** page.

items.q: My bar looks empty when I change form or stance.
items.a: It’s that form’s own bar, which the game keeps separate. Alfa lets you know and fills it with your abilities in one click (**Fill my bar**), only in empty slots.
Yes, and it always will be. It’s free software, with no ads, and nothing it does posts on its own in other players’ chat.

capitulos.lema: Tell us and we’ll fix it.

bloques.texto: Alfa is tested before every version, but WoW Forever is big and something always slips through. If you spot a bug or have an idea, the pack wants to know.

items: Type `/reload` to reload the interface.
Make sure Alfa is up to date: open **Instalar-Alfa.exe** again.
If a page looks off, try **Reset page**.
Bug, or is that how it works? Ask Lya (`/alfa ayuda`). Game running slow? `/alfa rendimiento` tells you how much memory and CPU each part of Alfa uses.
`/alfa diagnostico` (**Check Alfa**) looks for addons that clash with Alfa, parts turned off or from another version and odd settings, each with a one-click fix.
Alfa keeps its own errors: see them in **Settings > Style and sound > Caught errors**, to copy or clear them.
Lost your settings? Go back to one of your backups in **Settings > Style and sound > Backups**.

bloques.texto: Report with /alfa reportar

bloques.pie: The report builds itself as you type.

items: Type `/alfa reportar`.
Choose **Bug**, **Idea** or **Comment** and describe it in your own words.
Alfa adds what helps fix it: the version, the language, your class and level, where you are and the errors it caught. It doesn’t include your name or realm.
Press **Select all**, copy with [[Ctrl]]+[[C]] and paste it in the **#buzon-alfa** channel on La Jauría’s Discord.

bloques.texto: That mailbox is private: only Alfa’s developer reads what you send.
Come play with the pack, ask for help and hear about every new version.
You can also tell us in the CurseForge comments or open a report on GitHub: https://github.com/toxic3000/alfa-forever/issues
Thanks for letting us know! Every report helps make Alfa better for the whole pack.

items: **One Alfa menu:** the minimap icon, the addon list, the floating button and the **Alfa** button in the [[Esc]] menu all do the same. Click opens the last page you saw; right-click, the menu with every section.
**Combat stays out of the way when solo:** the interrupt sound and the fight summary show in a group, in instances or in long fights.
**Healing without a group:** “See how they look” shows your frames before you join one.
**The map:** the layers have one name everywhere, “Alfa layers”, and “Go to the game’s map” opens where you are.
**La Jauría:** a short announcement tells you when a pack wolf who uses Alfa is nearby, and meetups and notes no longer ask you to share your location.
